transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-19
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marco Alvarez (Redwood Product), Samantha Cho (Aurora PM), Ethan Park (Cloud Integration Lead), Ravi Singh (Solutions Architect)

Summary (auto): quick alignment on partner listing + reference arch, checklist for security/compliance, and next steps for benchmarks + assets.

[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): hey everyone thanks for joining i think we have about an hour, appreciate you all making time. quick intros?
[00:10] Samantha (Aurora PM): yeah i'm samantha, i run partner programs at auroracloud, happy to kick off.
[00:15] Ethan (Aurora): ethan here, lead on marketplace integrations and infra.
[00:18] Ravi (Aurora): ravi, solutions architect, i'll own the terraform and onboarding side.
[00:22] Jordan: great, from redwood we have priya se who've been working on the private deployment flow and marco on product to help with packaging.
[00:29] Priya (Redwood SE): hi all, i'll jump into the arch details later but quick note - our private offering supports both VPC peering and hosted private control plane in aurora region.
[00:38] Marco (Redwood Product): and i'll speak to the joint-solution artifacts and the marketplace requirements.

[02:05] Samantha: high level ask is: we want a clean marketplace listing on aurora with a supported reference architecture so customers can deploy redwood inference with our managed network and billing. what artifacts do you need from redwood?
[02:20] Jordan: good q; typically we provide a reference architecture diagram, terraform modules, sample deployment manifests, an install/run book, and a joint solution one-pager. also security docs - SOC2, encryption details, KMS, audit logs.
[02:38] Ethan: for marketplace we have a checklist - tech spec, pricing tiers, support SLAs, and legal MSA contact. i'll share the checklist after this call.

[04:12] Priya: on the arch front, important callouts: network topology (VPC peering versus private link), KV cache requirements for low latency chat workloads, GPU sizing guidance (we recommend at least one p4-equivalent node for initial pilot, but that's conversational guidance), and quantization profiles for smaller instances.
[04:40] Ravi: can you clarify the kv cache comment - is that the model kv cache or some redis prefix cache?
[04:45] Priya: good catch, sorry i mean the model KV cache (the attention key-value cache) - we also optionally support redis for session prefix caching. sometimes docs conflate the two so we'll spell that out.

[06:10] Marco: for the marketplace listing we should decide if we list as "Managed by AuroraCloud" with Redwood as an integration or list as a joint offering. that affects support boundaries and billing flow.
[06:28] Samantha: prefer joint offering — customers like a single click deploy with aurora-managed infra + redwood runtime. but we'll need a clear support matrix.
[06:38] Jordan: support matrix is doable. typical pattern: aurora handles infra/network, redwood handles model/runtime and inference SLAs, both share escalation path. we'll document runbooks and oncall contacts.

[08:02] Ethan: security/compliance question - does redwood support customer-managed KMS in private deployments and can keys be rotated by customer?
[08:14] Priya: yes, in our private control plane we integrate with customer KMS (KMS or HSM). keys can be customer-managed, rotateable. audit logs are shipped to the customer's log collection endpoint.
[08:28] Ravi: do you produce an attestable SOC2 artifact for the private deployment or only for hosted?
[08:34] Marco: we have SOC2 for the hosted control plane; for private we provide an architecture security kit and a SOC2 equivalency checklist plus instrumentation to capture audit logs for the customer's audit. we'll share the doc but legal may still request deeper attestation.

[10:45] Ethan: networking wise, we need terraform examples for vpc peering and route tables. also any specific ports for model serving pods?
[10:55] Priya: we'll add terraform snippets in the repo; ports are mostly standard HTTP/GRPC on 8080/443 plus metrics/health ports. we'll include an example security group policy.

[13:05] Samantha: for the reference arch diagram can we include an option for on-prem connector vs VPC peering? some customers want private airgapped.
[13:18] Pria (sic): sorry priya, i mean Priya — yes we have an on-prem package but it requires additional ops support; recommend target customers for on-prem are regulated verticals.
[13:33] Ravi: noted, we have a few prospects that will need air-gap details.

[15:02] Marco: on packaging, we should produce a terraform module and a helm chart variant for aurora managed k8s. also a marketplace image or listing that points to quickstart repo.
[15:17] Samantha: what's the expected install time? customers like 15-30 minutes for small pilots.
[15:23] Priya: small pilot with prebuilt images and our optimized quantized model can be 20-30 minutes in a well-provisioned cluster. full production with dedicated pools and autoscaling config takes longer and we recommend a 2-3 week onboarding for enterprises.

[17:50] Ethan: benchmarks — will redwood run a sample throughput/latency benchmark on aurora infra? we want to show perf numbers on the marketplace page.
[17:58] Jordan: yes. action: schedule a run in your staging region with our SE to execute a standardized benchmark (we have a spreadsheet for test cases). we'll need sample dataset, target sequence lengths, and concurrency.
[18:12] Samantha: we'll collate sample workloads and share.

[20:30] Ravi: how do fallbacks work? if aurora capacity is constrained can requests fall back to hosted redwood to maintain SLA?
[20:42] Priya: yes we have smart routing and fallback policies; customers can opt into cross-region or hosted fallback. that's a config option and we'll document the data residency/privacy implications.

[23:00] Marco: about billing — single invoice via aurora is easiest for GTM, but requires a reseller agreement. if separate billing, we can provide usage reports and token-level cost breakdowns for customers.
[23:15] Samantha: let's start with joint listing and single invoice as preferred go-to-market. legal will follow up on reseller terms.

[25:40] Ethan: request for artifacts list so aurora PM can track: 1) reference arch diagram 2) terraform module 3) helm chart 4) security checklist 5) joint one-pager 6) benchmark plan 7) pricing tiers 8) support matrix 9) sample listing text
[25:58] Jordan: validated — we'll deliver those items.

[28:10] Priya: quick tech note on quantization — some of our recommended quant profiles for 8-bit will reduce GPU memory by ~2-3x but could increase latency slightly on certain seq lengths; we'll provide recommended profiles by workload class.
[28:28] Ravi: good to know. we'll surface that in the marketplace FAQ.

[31:05] Samantha: legal/compliance handoff — who should aurora give the contract questions to at redwood?
[31:12] Jordan: send to contracts@redwood.inference (we'll paste contact) and cc me; marco will help with solution scoping docs.

[33:40] Marco: on the joint solution one-pager i'll draft a go-to-market blurb, list of supported scenarios, and a simple diagram. want to align on target verticals — we were thinking fintech and healthcare for initial push.
[33:54] Samantha: agree fintech and healthcare make sense; aurora has compliance certifications that help in those verticals.

[36:22] Ethan: technical deep dive follow-up: priya and ravi will collaborate on terraform module. can we pair-week next week?
[36:31] Ravi: yes, i'll block time for pairing.

[38:05] Priya: we've got a staging repo where we'll push the example helm chart and tf module; link will be shared in the notes. small caveat: some k8s operators require kernel flags for GPU drivers — we'll call that out so aurora can pre-provision nodes correctly.

[40:50] Samantha: marketplace screenshot assets — do you need animated gifs of quick deploy or static screenshots?
[40:57] Marco: static screenshots and a short 30s gif showing click-to-deploy are ideal. we'll produce both.

[43:12] Ethan: support SLOs — what's redwood's expected p99 latency target per model?
[43:20] Priya: depends on model and instance class; for our recommended production configs p95 is typically sub-300ms for small chat models and p99 targeted under 800ms on optimized GPU pools. we'll provide expected SLO table by config.

[45:55] Jordan: risk/mitigation thought — customers might be concerned about DR/backup for private control plane. we should include a runbook for failover and data retention.
[46:05] Marco: agree, we'll add DR playbook.

[48:20] Ravi: any gotchas with RBAC? we need to map aurora IAM to redwood roles for cross-account access.
[48:30] Priya: we support OIDC and SAML for identity federation and an RBAC mapping layer; we'll include sample IAM policies and instructions for mapping roles.

[50:08] Samantha: timing wise what's a reasonable public listing ETA once artifacts and legal are done?
[50:16] Jordan: typically 2-3 weeks after we have all artifacts and a signed partner addendum. if we fast-track and legal moves quickly it can be two weeks.

[52:55] Ethan: ok let's recap actions.
[53:00] Jordan: recap: redwood will share reference arch, terraform examples, helm chart, security checklist, SLO table, joint one-pager, and benchmark spreadsheet. aurora will share marketplace checklist, legal contacts, and staging credentials for benchmark. schedule benchmark week of 11/23. pairing session for terraform next week.
[53:25] Samantha: perfect - thanks everyone.
[55:30] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites and links. bye.

End of transcript.
